events.title: The Arno floods Florence
events.description: After days of heavy rain, the Arno burst its banks and swept away three of Florence's four bridges, including the Ponte Vecchio. The chronicler Giovanni Villani recorded the disaster in detail.

events.title: Paganino Doria captures the Venetian fleet at Sapienza
events.description: In the War of the Straits, the Genoese fleet under Paganino Doria defeated and captured the entire Venetian fleet of Niccolò Pisani in the Battle of Sapienza, also called Porto Longo. The war between the two maritime republics ended in 1355.

events.title: Joan of Arc takes Saint-Pierre-le-Moûtier
events.description: After a first assault on the heavily fortified, moated town of Saint-Pierre-le-Moûtier failed, Joan of Arc launched a second that, according to her bodyguard Jean d'Aulon, met little resistance, and the town was taken.

events.title: Catherine of Aragon meets Arthur, Prince of Wales
events.description: Catherine of Aragon, aged 15, met Arthur, Prince of Wales, the eldest son of Henry VII, at Dogmersfield in Hampshire. They married ten days later; after Arthur's death she became the first wife of his younger brother, Henry VIII.

events.title: The Northwestern Confederacy destroys St Clair's army on the Wabash
events.description: The Northwestern Confederacy of Native Americans destroyed a United States army under St Clair in the Northwest Territory. Also called the Battle of a Thousand Slain, it has been described as the most decisive defeat in the history of the American military.

events.title: Forrest's cavalry strike the Union supply base at Johnsonville
events.description: Ending a 23-day raid through western Tennessee, Confederate cavalry under Nathan Bedford Forrest destroyed 28 Union boats and barges and millions of dollars of supplies at Johnsonville. It hampered George H. Thomas's plans against Hood's invasion of Tennessee.

events.title: The poet Wilfred Owen is killed in action
events.description: Wilfred Owen was killed crossing the Sambre-Oise Canal in France, a week before the armistice. His poems, including 'Dulce et Decorum Est', became the defining English verse of the First World War.
events.html: Wilfred Owen was killed crossing the Sambre-Oise Canal in France, a week before the armistice. His poems, including 'Dulce et Decorum Est', became the defining English verse of the First World War.

events.title: Howard Carter finds the steps to Tutankhamun's tomb
events.description: Howard Carter's workers uncovered a step cut into the rock of the Valley of the Kings, leading to the nearly intact tomb of Tutankhamun. Its treasures caused a worldwide sensation.
events.html: Howard Carter's workers uncovered a step cut into the rock of the Valley of the Kings, leading to the nearly intact tomb of Tutankhamun. Its treasures caused a worldwide sensation.

events.title: Soviet tanks move in to crush the Hungarian Revolution
events.description: Soviet forces launched a massive assault on Budapest at dawn, overthrowing Imre Nagy's government. Thousands were killed, and the West did not intervene.
events.html: Soviet forces launched a massive assault on Budapest at dawn, overthrowing Imre Nagy's government. Thousands were killed, and the West did not intervene.

events.title: Students seize the US embassy in Tehran
events.description: Iranian students occupied the US embassy in Tehran and took 66 hostages. Fifty-two were held for 444 days, a crisis that soured US-Iranian relations and damaged Jimmy Carter's presidency.

events.title: Barack Obama is elected president
events.description: Barack Obama defeated John McCain to become the first African American elected president of the United States, 45 years after Martin Luther King's 'I Have a Dream' speech.
events.html: Barack Obama defeated John McCain to become the first African American elected president of the United States, 45 years after Martin Luther King's 'I Have a Dream' speech.

song: Americans of the First World War
A cheerful American marching song of 1917, written to get young men to join the army in the First World War.
